text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx errors from model-serving-runtime (us-east-1c). 1m error rate > 15% and p95 latency degraded. Affected route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-13b-v1). link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/2113006789

Alice M: seeing this too — dashboards show a sharp increase in 'model_runner_crash_total' and OOM kill events on node pool 'infer-gpu-pool-3'.

Bob R: paging infra oncall @Dave (infra) — can you take?

Dave (infra): taking. quick overview: pods for model-runner are restarting with SIGSEGV and occasionally OOMKilled. core dumps on node-3b-12.

Carol L: customer impact: several PLG customers report 5xxs, we have 7 active tenants with >10% error rate, one enterprise complaining to CSM.

Eve S: tagging SRE and support. putting status page draft: "Degraded: inference API experiencing elevated 5xx for some models" — okay to publish? :warning:

Dave (infra): yes publish. immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic away from us-east-1c to other regions 2) scale down concurrent in-flight requests for the model 3) apply node drain + reboot to clear bad kernel state 4) if that fails, route traffic to fallback model variant (smaller/quantized).

Alice M: can we do an automated routing rule now? I can flip a policy to route new requests to redwood-13b-v1-quantized-8bit in the control plane. That will preserve semantics for most calls.

Dave (infra): please do that. also reduce max_concurrent_requests for that model on the runtime to 2 per worker:
```yaml
model_config:
  name: redwood-13b-v1
  max_concurrent_requests: 2
  request_timeout_ms: 60000
```

Carol L: CSM notified customers A, B, C. estimating 30-40% of requests hit the affected pool based on request tags.

Bob R: oncall handoff: @oncall is now owning the incident post-mitigation. Dave, want handoff once routing changes are live?

Dave (infra): yes — I'll execute the steps and report back. starting with traffic drain. running kubectl drain on nodes with high crash counts. commands:
```
# list pods with restarts > 3 in last 10m
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running | awk '{print $1,$3,$6}'
# drain node
kubectl drain node/node-3b-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

incident-bot: NOTE: recent deploy 2026-03-15T03:12Z model-runner v2.4.1 promoted to us-east-1c ~40m ago.

Dave (infra): suspect regressions in v2.4.1 — candidates: memory growth in attention cache, small race in kvcache access causing segfault. I'm pulling core dumps now.

Alice M: sharing stack trace snippet from core:
```
# backtrace
#0 0x7f8a3c0f in kvcache_get (kv=0x7f..) at kvcache.cc:274
#1 0x7f8a4b2d in run_inference at runner.cc:1032
#2 0x7f8a4c01 in thread_entry at threadpool.cc:58
```

Eve S: operational impact note for status page: "We are investigating runtime crashes causing elevated 5xxs; traffic has been partially rerouted and we are performing rolling restarts. Some requests may receive slower fallbacks."

Bob R: update: Alice completed the control plane routing switch to quantized model variant and reduced concurrency limits. Traffic to affected pool dropped by ~75% according to routing metrics.

Dave (infra): draining nodes now. performed reboot on node-3b-12 after collecting cores. reboot completed. monitoring for new crashes.

Carol L: support report: customer D continues to see errors even after switch, they are pinned to specific region — offering to move them to dedicated capacity as temporary measure.

Alice M: looking at logs after switch: 5xxs decreased to baseline for most tenants, but a steady 1-2% 5xx remains from long-sequence requests that exceed new memory threshold. Could add soft-rejection for sequences > 4096 tokens to avoid OOM.

Dave (infra): applying a temporary request filter at the edge: reject requests with input_length > 4096 with 429 and suggestion to paginate. config change:
```
route_filters:
  - name: long_seq_reject
    condition: input.tokens > 4096
    action: reject
    status_code: 429
```

incident-bot: AUTOMATION: created a hotfix branch and a rollback candidate for model-runner -> v2.4.0. tag: rollback/v2.4.1.

Dave (infra): initial hypothesis seems confirmed: a regression in memory management in v2.4.1 under specific batch/sequence combos. plan after stabilization: roll back v2.4.1 in us-east-1c and run stress tests. For now, continue draining and patching routes.

Bob R: can we get numbers for customer impact for postmortem? Need: total requests, 5xx count by tenant, time window, number of restarts, nodes affected. Carol, can you coordinate with support to gather?

Carol L: on it. will export from BigQuery and Slack logs, share link to docs: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2113006789-postmortem-draft (draft in progress).

Eve S: legal and trust notified. any PII risk? No. all logs scrubbed.

Alice M: monitoring shows metrics improving. p95 latency back to normal and error rate <1.5% cluster-wide. the affected node pool shows no new segfaults after restart.

Dave (infra): rolling rollback scheduled in 15m to v2.4.0 on the remaining us-east-1c runners. will keep canary of 5 pods for 10m before full rollout. commands:
```
# rollback deployment
kubectl set image deploy/model-runner model-runner=redwood/model-runner:v2.4.0 -n inference
# monitor
kubectl rollout status deploy/model-runner -n inference --watch
```

Bob R: thanks team. after rollback and traffic stabilization, I'll mark P0 incident to resolved and start timeline for postmortem. please keep channel updated with any regressions.

Dave (infra): rollback canary healthy. no new segfaults in canary after 12m. proceeding with full rollout.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: error rate returned to normal in us-east-1c. Incident closed for now; postmortem required.

Carol L: saving notes and next steps: 1) postmortem with timeline + root cause (v2.4.1 memory regression) 2) better canary thresholds for crashes and OOM 3) add per-model max_sequence soft limits and better control plane flags 4) alert refinement to include 'crash_count' anomaly and auto-reroute policy.

Alice M: I'll open PR for short-term control plane flags and add a unit test for kvcache concurrent access.

Eve S: status page updated to reflect mitigations and closure. customers notified with RCA pending. :white_check_mark:

Bob R: handoff complete. great job. closing thread once postmortem link posted.

Carol L: postmortem draft available: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2113006789-postmortem-draft — adding metrics + tenant impact table now.

Alice M: adding reproduction harness to ci/inference/regressions. QA please run the stress-suite against v2.4.1 vs v2.4.0.

Dave (infra): final note: we collected 4 core dumps and corresponding metrics windows. attaching artifacts to incident: s3://incidents/2113006789/cores/ (internal).
